description: Early-game unit (mostly ply <= 12), on my turn right after the opponent stacked: strongest when the opponent has two or three stones stacked on top of column 6 (rightmost), especially with columns 1 and 5 still empty, an opponent stone at the bottom of column 2 and mine at the bottom of column 3. An opponent stone at the bottom of column 3 or my stones in columns 0-1 suppress it. Weak, context-dependent; not a single clean concept.
effect: None measurable: forcing it to max or zero changes move probabilities by <= 0.07 (usually 0.00) on 7 positions.
notes: H1 opp top-run>=2 in col 6: F1 0.17-0.21. Column-weighted vertical pairs: 0.20. Bottom-row template (col6 O stack, cols 1/5 empty, (0,6)O,(0,2)O,(0,3)X, ply fade): 0.27; plus (0,3)=O penalty and col0/2 O pairs: best F1 0.306, AUROC 0.63, sim share 0.10. Minimal pairs show strong context dependence (same col-6 stack 4.5 vs -0.6 depending on my stones). Possibly a distributed/random direction. One score call was wasted on a duplicate run.
